metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive pessimism.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 1–2% in next 3–5 days to align with mean reversion.  
- If sentiment turns positive (avg > 0.3) after prolonged negative trend, model underreacts; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile (±0.3–0.7) — add 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast to account for sentiment-driven volatility.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.2–0.3), model often lags 1–2 days behind true price — shift forecast 1–2 days ahead with slight upward bias to capture momentum.
